uncited: GeoGaussian modifies the standard densification and optimization pipeline of 3D Gaussian Splatting.

It retains the primitive definition of position $\mathbf{p}_i$, covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$ (parameterized by rotation $\mathbf{R}_i$ and scale $\mathbf{s}_i$), opacity $\alpha_i$, and color $\mathbf{c}_i$ [Parent].
- Current set of 3D Gaussians $\mathcal{G} = \{G_i\}$.
- Gradient information from the rendering loss.
- Updated set of 3D Gaussians with improved geometric coherence.
- Each Gaussian $i$ stores its position $\mathbf{p}_i$, rotation matrix $\mathbf{R}_i$, scale vector $\mathbf{s}_i$, opacity $\alpha_i$, and color coefficients $\mathbf{c}_i$.
- The covariance matrix is $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i = \mathbf{R}_i \mathbf{S}_i \mathbf{S}_i^T \mathbf{R}_i^T$, where $\mathbf{S}_i = \text{diag}(\mathbf{s}_i)$ [Parent].
**Tangent Plane Densification:** When a Gaussian $i$ requires densification (based on standard gradient thresholds), new Gaussians are not spawned randomly or uniformly in space.
Instead, they are placed on the tangent plane of the parent Gaussian $i$.
The tangent plane is defined by the normal vector $\mathbf{n}_i$ derived from the orientation of $\mathbf{R}_i$.
**Geometric Smoothness Regularization:** To encourage smoothness of geometric properties between neighboring Gaussians, a regularization term is added to the loss function.
This term penalizes large differences in normals or positions between adjacent Gaussians.
Let $\mathcal{N}(i)$ be the set of neighbors of Gaussian $i$.
**Optimization:** The total loss is the sum of the rendering loss (photometric error) and the geometric smoothness loss.
